He candidly submits that the actions of the respondents suffers from gross malice in fact and malice in law as has been settled in the case of Dr. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh reported in 33 DLR (AD) 201, inasmuch as the impugned actions of the respondents taken against the petitioners demonstrate and wrongful act done intentionally without just cause and the facts and circumstances of the issues constitute malice in law inasmuch as the wrongful act done intentionally, without just cause or excuse in total disregard of the principle of the rule of law, fundamental rights and ratio settled in different cases by our apex court including the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST, reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63 and, as such„ the impugned actions of the respondents are liable to be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respondents are required to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in the said arbitrary and mala fide lodging of cases against the petitioners. 

 43. He lastly submits that in the given facts and circumstances, it has become a Frankenstein of the law enforcement agencies not only to abuse its power violating the fundamental rights of the citizens but also to undermine and disregard the guidelines given by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST, reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63 and if this is allowed to be continued, the basic structure of the Constitution, being the supremacy of the constitution, independence of judiciary in general and Article 111 of the Constitution in particular may be undermined and thus the democracy, rule of law, and independence of judiciary will be allowed to be violated and, as such„ the impugned actions of the respondents are liable to be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respondents are required to be directed to take appropriate legal actions against the officers, who are involved in the said arbitrary and mala fide lodging of cases against the petitioners. 

 48. I have gone through the applications filed by the petitioners under Article 102 of the Constitution and the materials annexed thereto. I have also considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the learned Attorney-General for Bangladesh. I have also considered their submissions to the best of my wit and wisdom. From the writ petition, it is noticeable that the petitioners have challenged the arbitrary and mala fide actions of the respondents committed through police officers under their control and supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and others and they have also prayed for direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in lodging of arbitrary, mala fide and fictitious cases against the petitioners and others. From the cause title and the prayer portion of the writ petition, it is clear that the petitioners have basically challenged the criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others under writ jurisdiction. The actions of police officers and the respondents are meant for criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others. It appears from the record that the petitioners are the accused of some cases of Paltan Model Police station and Mirpur Model Police station. It is evident from the record that the facts of some cases were published in different newspapers. On going through the FIR, it appears that some specific facts and offences narrating the chaotic situation in different roads of Dhaka City have been disclosed in those FIR. It may be stated that the facts and offences disclosed in the FIR are highly contentious and disputed question of fact. The truthfulness or falsehood of the allegations can be looked into by the investigating officers and the learned judges of the Court below at the time of framing charge and after recording evidence from the respective parties. The truthfulness and/or falsehood of the allegations cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. If there is any illegality or irregularity in the cases, that can be addressed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure if so challenged by the aggrieved person/s. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this writ petition is not maintainable in the eye of law. It is stated in the application that some cases have been filed against the dead person and the persons who were in abroad at the time of incidents and the very facts have been published in different newspapers. Basing on the aforesaid news, the petitioners have approached this Court challenging the actions of cases taken against them. It has been decided in a series of case laws that the disputed question of facts can be decided in writ jurisdiction. It is now well settled that newspaper reports cannot be admitted into evidence unless the correspondent of such a report comes to the witness box to vouchsafe in support of the report on oath. The aforesaid view finds support in the decision in the case of Osena Begum alias Babuler Ma vs State, reported in 55 DLR 299.
